mainTopic: Overpaying for a yoke, and which of a donkey's equipment is sold with the donkey
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier case: a buyer paid a very high price for a yoke, and the רבנן said the price does not prove the oxen were included. The גמרא asks why the sale is not then cancelled for overcharging. It gives two answers: the sale really is cancelled, or the overpayment was so obvious that it counts as a gift. Then a new משנה asks whether a donkey's equipment is sold with the donkey. The תנא קמא says no, נחום המדי says yes, and רבי יהודה says it depends on how the buyer asked. עולא explains that the argument is only about load gear (sack, saddlebag, כומני), while the saddle and similar gear are sold according to everyone. The גמרא defends עולא from a ברייתא and explains that a כומני is a women's riding seat. Finally, it asks whether the argument is about gear on the donkey or gear off it. It tries proofs from the ברייתא and from רבי יהודה, and the rejection of the second proof continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Don't the רבנן accept cancelling a sale for overcharging?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the view that the רבנן ignore the overpayment. It proves from a משנה in בבא מציעא that the רבנן fully accept the laws of אונאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say the רבנן don't hold of cancelling a sale for overcharging, is that really so? But we learned in a משנה: רבי יהודה says, one who sells a ספר תורה, an animal, or a pearl has no אונאה. They said to him: the חכמים only listed these (land, slaves and documents)!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is still on the earlier case of the yoke sold for a very high price. It asks: if the רבנן say the price proves nothing, the buyer was overcharged, so the sale should be cancelled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might suggest the רבנן simply don't accept ביטול מקח. The גמרא rejects that. In the משנה in בבא מציעא, the רבנן argue with רבי יהודה and say even a ספר תורה, an animal or a pearl IS subject to אונאה. So the רבנן clearly accept the laws of overcharging, and the question stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Cancelling the sale. This applies when the price is off by more than one-sixth.
Overcharging or underpaying compared to the market price
'And if you would say', which introduces a possible suggestion
A pearl

phrases.english: And if you would say that cancelling the sale
the Rabbis do not accept, do they really not?!
But didn't we learn: Rabbi Yehuda says:
One who sells a Torah scroll, an animal, or a pearl,
these have no law of overcharging.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: לֹא אָמְרוּ אֶלָּא אֶת אֵלּוּ!
phrases.english: They said to him: They said this only about these!
phrases.notes: 'These' means the items listed earlier in that משנה: land, slaves and documents.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא בִּיטּוּל מִקָּח לְרַבָּנַן לֵית לְהוּ, וְלָא?! וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the discussion from the previous section about the yoke sold at an inflated price.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the רבנן do not apply ביטול מקח to the overpriced yoke
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The רבנן extend אונאה even to a Torah scroll, an animal and a pearl, so they surely accept ביטול מקח. The overpriced yoke sale should therefore be cancelled.

steps.title: 'The price is no proof' means the sale is cancelled
steps.stepSummary: First answer: when the רבנן said 'אין דמים ראיה', they meant the sale is cancelled.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is meant by 'the money is no proof' that the משנה teaches? That the sale is cancelled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the רבנן agree with the question. Their words 'the price is no proof' actually mean the sale is cancelled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no contradiction. The high price does not show that the oxen were included. Since the buyer got only the yoke for far too much money, the sale is cancelled under the rule of ביטול מקח.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The price is no proof', the רבנן's words in the earlier משנה
'What?', here meaning 'what is meant by?'
'That it teaches', referring to the משנה's wording

phrases.english: What is meant by 'the money is no proof'
that it also teaches?
That it is a cancelled sale.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the wording of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'The price is no proof' seemed to mean the sale stands for the yoke alone at the high price.
steps.terutzMaskana: It means the sale is cancelled because of the overcharge.

steps.title: A huge overpayment counts as a gift
steps.stepSummary: Second answer: אונאה only applies to a price gap a person could be fooled by. A gap so large that nobody would mistake it is treated as a gift.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or if you want, say: when the רבנן spoke of overcharging and cancelling a sale, they meant an amount a person could mistake. But an amount nobody could mistake is not included. We say he gave it to him as a gift.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a different answer. Here the sale stands, because the overpayment was too obvious to be a mistake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The laws of אונאה protect someone who honestly did not know the real price. If the price gap is so big that no one could miss it, the buyer knew what he was doing. So the extra money is a present to the seller, not a cheat.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And if you wish, say', which introduces a second answer
An amount a person could be mistaken about
A gift

steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers for the רבנן. Either the yoke sale is cancelled, or the overpayment is so obvious that it counts as a gift, because אונאה only covers mistakes a person could actually make.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אֲמוּר רַבָּנַן אוֹנָאָה וּבִיטּוּל מִקָּח –
phrases.english: When the Rabbis spoke of overcharging and cancelling a sale,
it was about an amount a person could be mistaken about,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל בִּכְדֵי שֶׁאֵין הַדַּעַת טוֹעָה – לָא;
phrases.english: but about an amount a person could not be mistaken about, no;
say that he gave it to him as a gift.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: כִּי אֲמוּר רַבָּנַן אוֹנָאָה וּבִיטּוּל מִקָּח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, different answer to the challenge of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every overcharge of more than a sixth cancels the sale.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a gap a person could mistake counts as אונאה. An obvious, huge gap is a gift, so the sale stands.

steps.title: Selling a donkey: is its equipment included?
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה. The תנא קמא says the donkey's equipment is not sold with it, and נחום המדי says it is.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One who sells a donkey has not sold its equipment. נחום המדי says: he has sold its equipment.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins with a new משנה about what is included when a donkey is sold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two views argue about what a plain sale of a donkey covers. The תנא קמא says the buyer gets only the animal. נחום המדי says the equipment goes with it.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מתניתין, 'our משנה'
A donkey
Its 'vessels', meaning its equipment and gear
נחום from מדי (Media), a תנא

phrases.english: MISHNA: One who sells the donkey
has not sold its equipment.
Nachum the Mede says: He has sold its equipment.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַמּוֹכֵר אֶת הַחֲמוֹר – לֹא מָכַר כֵּלָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה and a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תנא קמא: the equipment is not sold. נחום המדי: it is sold.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: it depends on how the buyer asked
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says the equipment is sometimes sold and sometimes not. It depends on the buyer's words while the loaded donkey stands in front of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: sometimes it is sold and sometimes not. How so? The donkey was in front of him with its equipment on it. If the buyer said 'Sell me this donkey of yours', the equipment is sold. If he said 'Is it your donkey?', the equipment is not sold.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a third, in-between opinion that depends on how the buyer phrased his request.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the buyer points to 'this donkey' as it stands, loaded with its gear, he means the whole package. When he only asks 'Is the donkey yours?', he shows interest in the animal itself, so the gear is not included.

keyTerms.meaning: Sometimes
How so?
Sold

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
Sometimes they are sold, sometimes they are not sold.
How so? If the donkey was in front of him
and its equipment was on it, and he said to him:
'Sell me this donkey of yours',
then its equipment is sold.
'Is it your donkey?', then its equipment is not sold.
phrases.notes: The buyer is just asking whether the donkey belongs to him, as an opening to buying it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: פְּעָמִים מְכוּרִין, פְּעָמִים אֵינָן מְכוּרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third opinion to the dispute in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'Sell me this donkey' includes the equipment. 'Is it your donkey?' does not.

steps.title: עולא: the dispute is only about the carrying gear
steps.stepSummary: עולא limits the argument to load-carrying items: the sack, the saddlebag and the כומני. The disagreement is whether a typical donkey is for riding or for carrying. Gear used for both is sold according to everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: the dispute is about the sack, the saddlebag and the כומני. The תנא קמא holds that a typical donkey is for riding. נחום המדי holds that a typical donkey is for carrying loads. But the saddle, the saddlecloth, the harness and the saddle band are sold according to everyone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with עולא defining exactly which equipment the משנה's argument is about, and why they argue.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each side has a different picture of an ordinary donkey. If it is mainly for riding, load gear is extra and is not sold. If it is mainly for carrying, the load gear is part of it. Saddle-type gear serves both uses, so everyone agrees it is sold.

keyTerms.meaning: A dispute
An ordinary, typical donkey
A load, or carrying burdens
A saddle
Everyone agrees
The first, unnamed opinion in the משנה

steps.whatToRemember: According to עולא, the argument is only about load-carrying gear: whether a typical donkey is for riding or for carrying. Gear that serves both purposes goes with the donkey according to everyone.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the תנא קמא holds that no equipment at all is sold. According to עולא, even the תנא קמא agrees that the saddle and similar gear are sold.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Ulla said:
The dispute is about the sack, the saddlebag and the kumni,
for the first Tanna holds:
an ordinary donkey stands for riding,
and Nachum the Mede holds:
an ordinary donkey stands for carrying loads;
but the saddle and the saddlecloth, the harness and the saddle band,
everyone agrees they are sold.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר עוּלָּא: מַחֲלוֹקֶת בְּשַׂק וְדִיסַקַּיָּא וְכוּמְנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the scope of the dispute in the משנה (step 4).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute covers only load-carrying gear. Gear used for both riding and carrying is sold according to everyone.

steps.title: A ברייתא seems to say the saddle is sold only when the seller mentions the gear
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists what is sold when someone says 'a donkey and its gear.' It seems to mean that without those words, even the saddle and saddlecloth are not sold. That goes against עולא.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged from a ברייתא: If the seller says 'I am selling you a donkey and its gear,' he has sold the saddle, the saddlecloth, the harness and the saddle band. He has not sold the sack, the saddlebag or the כומני. If he said 'it and everything on it,' all of them are sold. So the buyer gets the saddle and saddlecloth only because the seller said 'a donkey and its gear.' If he did not say that, the buyer does not get them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to challenge what עולא said in step 6.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא said that gear used both for riding and for carrying, like the saddle and saddlecloth, is sold according to everyone, even if the seller says only 'a donkey.' The ברייתא gives those items to the buyer only when the seller said 'a donkey and its gear.' That suggests a plain 'donkey' sale does not include them, which goes against עולא.

keyTerms.meaning: Saddle
Saddlecloth or padding under the saddle
Harness strap
Saddle band that goes around the belly
Saddlebag

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
'I am selling you a donkey and its gear' –
this one has sold the saddle,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֶת הַמַּרְדַּעַת, וְאֶת הַקִּילְקְלִי, וְאֶת הַחֲבָק.
phrases.english: and the saddlecloth, and the harness, and the saddle band.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל לֹא מָכַר שַׂק, וְדִיסַקַּיָּא, וְכוּמְנִי.
phrases.english: But he did not sell the sack, the saddlebag, or the כומני.

phrases.aramaic: וּבִזְמַן שֶׁאָמַר לוֹ: ״הִיא וְכֹל מַה שֶּׁעָלֶיהָ״ –
phrases.english: And when he said to him: 'It and everything that is on it' –
all of them are sold.
The reason is that he said to him 'a donkey and its gear' –
that is why he acquires the saddle and saddlecloth,

phrases.aramaic: הָא לָא אֲמַר לֵיהּ הָכִי – לָא!
phrases.english: but if he did not say that to him – he does not!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges עולא's claim that dual-use gear is sold according to everyone.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's statement that the saddle and saddlecloth are sold according to all opinions, even in a plain sale of a donkey.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא ties the sale of the saddle and saddlecloth to the words 'and its gear,' which suggests a plain sale does not include them.

steps.title: The ברייתא's real point is about the carrying gear
steps.stepSummary: Even without 'and its gear,' the saddle and saddlecloth are sold. The ברייתא's lesson is that even with those words, the sack, saddlebag and כומני are not sold.
steps.simpleTranslation: The same is true even if he did not say 'a donkey and its gear': the saddle and saddlecloth are still sold. The ברייתא is teaching us that even if he did say 'a donkey and its gear,' the buyer still does not get the sack, saddlebag and כומני.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends עולא by explaining what the ברייתא is really trying to teach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא did not mention 'and its gear' to show that the saddle needs those words. It mentioned them to show their limit: even such general words do not include the carrying gear. So the ברייתא and עולא agree.

keyTerms.meaning: The same law applies
This is what it teaches us
Even though

phrases.english: The same is true even though
he did not say to him 'a donkey and its gear' –
the saddle and saddlecloth are also sold;
and this is what it teaches us –

phrases.aramaic: דְּאַף עַל גַּב דַּאֲמַר לֵיהּ: ״חֲמוֹר וְכֵלָיו״ –
phrases.english: that even though he said to him 'a donkey and its gear' –
he does not acquire the sack, the saddlebag, or the כומני.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּא הַדִּין דְּאַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא אֲמַר לֵיהּ
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the ברייתא's purpose: it shows how far the words 'and its gear' reach, not what they are needed for.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The words 'and its gear' are what make the saddle and saddlecloth part of the sale.
steps.terutzMaskana: The saddle and saddlecloth are sold anyway. The words 'and its gear' still do not bring in the carrying gear.
steps.whatToRemember: Gear used for both riding and carrying, like the saddle and saddlecloth, goes with the donkey anyway. The sack, saddlebag and כומני are not sold even if the seller says 'and its gear.' They are sold only if he says 'it and everything on it.'

steps.title: What is a כומני?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the word כומני means.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask about an unclear word in the ברייתא. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sack and saddlebag are familiar, but כומני is not. The גמרא wants to know what this item is.

keyTerms.meaning: An item on the donkey; explained in the next step

phrases.english: What is 'and the כומני'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a word from the ברייתא quoted in step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the word כומני.

steps.title: A כומני is a women's riding seat
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא בר שמואל explains that a כומני is the riding seat women use.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא בר שמואל said: It is a riding seat for women.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא בר שמואל answers the question and tells us what a כומני is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כומני is a special seat for women. It belongs to the same group as the sack and saddlebag, which עולא said in step 6 are the items the תנא קמא and נחום המדי argue about.

keyTerms.meaning: A riding seat used by women

phrases.english: Rav Pappa bar Shmuel said:
A women's riding seat.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: כומני means a riding seat for women.

steps.title: Is the argument about gear on the donkey or gear off it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where the מחלוקת between the רבנן and נחום המדי applies. Is it when the gear is on the donkey, so נחום המדי agrees when it is off? Or is it when the gear is off, so the רבנן agree when it is on?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: Is the argument when the gear is on the donkey, but when it is not on it, נחום המדי agrees with the רבנן that it is not sold? Or maybe the argument is when the gear is not on the donkey, but when it is on it, the רבנן agree with נחום that it is sold?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question about the scope of the מחלוקת in the משנה from step 4.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two possible ways to frame the argument. Either נחום המדי sells the gear only when it is on the donkey, or the רבנן keep the gear back only when it is off the donkey. Each option has one side agreeing in one situation.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked before them (the חכמים)
While they (the gear) are on it (the donkey)
Agrees, admits the other side's view
Or perhaps

phrases.english: A question was asked of them:
Is the argument when they are on it,
but when they are not on it –
נחום המדי agrees with them;
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the רבנן, so here נחום agrees the gear is not sold.

phrases.english: or perhaps the argument is when they are not on it,
but when they are on it –
the רבנן agree with נחום?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the משנה's מחלוקת (step 4) and asks in which situation it applies.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the מחלוקת between the רבנן and נחום המדי is about gear on the donkey or gear off it.
steps.confusionAlert: Both sides of the question agree there is an argument. The only question is which situation it covers: gear on the donkey or gear off it.

steps.title: A proof from the ברייתא: 'it and everything on it'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings back the end of the ברייתא. If the seller says 'it and everything on it,' everything is sold.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: And when he said to him 'it and everything that is on it,' all of them are sold.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to try to answer the question from step 11.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's case speaks about gear that is on the donkey. This line is brought to shed light on what the law is when the gear is on the donkey. The גמרא will look at what exactly this source proves.

keyTerms.meaning: Everything that is on it

phrases.english: Come and hear:

phrases.aramaic: וּבִזְמַן שֶׁאָמַר לוֹ: ״הוּא וְכֹל מַה שֶּׁעָלָיו״ –
phrases.english: And when he said to him: 'It and everything that is on it' –
all of them are sold.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to settle the question of step 11 using the ברייתא from step 7.
steps.raayaObject: The question of whether the רבנן and נחום המדי argue about gear on the donkey or off it.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The end of the ברייתא: 'it and everything on it,' where all the gear is sold.

steps.title: Which opinion could the end of the ברייתא follow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא spells out the proof. If the מחלוקת is about gear still on the donkey, the end of the ברייתא follows the רבנן. If the מחלוקת is about gear taken off, then everyone agrees gear on the donkey is sold, and the ברייתא fits nobody.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well if you say the מחלוקת is about gear still on the donkey: then this ruling follows the רבנן. But if you say the מחלוקת is only about gear that has been taken off, and everyone agrees gear still on the donkey is sold, then whose opinion is this ruling?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof it began in Step 12. It shows that the end of the ברייתא only makes sense under the first option.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the first option, the רבנן hold that gear on the donkey is not sold automatically, so the seller had to say 'everything on it.' Under the second option, gear on the donkey is sold according to everyone, so that statement would be pointless. This puts pressure on the second option.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well / granted (this fits nicely)
While they (the gear) are still on it (the donkey)
Whose opinion is this?
Everyone agrees

phrases.english: It works well if you say
that the dispute is when the gear is still on it,
whose view is this? It is the Rabbis.
phrases.notes: For the רבנן, gear on the donkey is not included on its own, so the seller had to say 'everything on it.'

phrases.english: But if you say
that the dispute is when the gear is not on it,
but when the gear is still on it,
everyone agrees they are sold;
whose view is this?
phrases.notes: If the gear is sold anyway, there is no need for the seller to say 'everything on it.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the ending of the ברייתא quoted in Step 12 proves the first option.
steps.kashyaTarget: The second option from Step 11: that the מחלוקת is about gear that has been taken off.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under that option, gear on the donkey is sold according to everyone, so the ברייתא's need for an explicit 'everything on it' fits no opinion.

steps.title: Rereading the ברייתא as 'everything fit to be on it'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא keeps the second option. It changes the ברייתא's wording to 'it and everything that is fit to be on it,' which covers gear that is not on the donkey right now.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, the מחלוקת is about gear that has been taken off, and the ברייתא follows the רבנן. Read it this way: 'And when he said to him: it and everything that is fit to be on it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof by adjusting the wording of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the new wording, the seller is talking about gear that belongs on a donkey but is not on it now. The רבנן need an explicit statement for that kind of gear, so the ברייתא fits the second option after all.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / actually (holding on to the original position)
And say (read the text this way instead)
Fit to be on it: the kind of gear usually put on a donkey

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up 'everything on it' with 'everything fit to be on it.' The first is gear sitting on the donkey right now. The second covers gear that belongs on a donkey even if it was taken off.

phrases.english: Really, the dispute is when the gear is not on it,
and it is the Rabbis;
and say: and when he said to him:
phrases.notes: The גמרא is changing the ending of the ברייתא from Step 12. Read it with these new words.

phrases.english: 'It and everything that is fit to be on it.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof made in Steps 12 and 13.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the end of the ברייתא only.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof depended on the wording 'everything on it.' The ברייתא can be read as 'everything fit to be on it,' which removes the proof.

steps.title: A new proof from רבי יהודה in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries a new proof. רבי יהודה says the gear is sometimes sold and sometimes not. It suggests he is speaking about the same case as the תנא קמא, which would tell us what case the מחלוקת is about.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי יהודה says, 'Sometimes they are sold, sometimes they are not sold.' Isn't רבי יהודה talking about the same case as the תנא קמא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second attempt to answer the question from Step 11, this time from the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי יהודה is responding to the תנא קמא, they are discussing the same situation. If רבי יהודה's 'sometimes sold' case is gear on the donkey, then the main מחלוקת would be about gear on the donkey too.

keyTerms.meaning: Sometimes
Isn't it that…? (suggesting a reading of the source)
The first, unnamed opinion in the משנה
Stands on / is referring to

phrases.english: Come and hear: Rabbi Yehuda says:
Sometimes they are sold,
sometimes they are not sold.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי, לָאו אַמַּאי דְּקָאָמַר תַּנָּא קַמָּא
phrases.english: What, is it not about what the first tanna said
that Rabbi Yehuda is referring?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof was rejected, a new proof is brought for the same question.
steps.raayaObject: To show that the מחלוקת between the רבנן and נחום המדי is about gear still on the donkey.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהודה's statement in the משנה: 'sometimes they are sold, sometimes they are not sold.'

steps.title: The proof from רבי יהודה starts to be rejected
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to reject the proof by saying 'No, רבי יהודה…'. The rest of the rejection continues on the next amud (78b).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to push away the proof from רבי יהודה. The full answer comes right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'No' tells us the גמרא does not accept that רבי יהודה must be talking about the same case as the תנא קמא. How it explains רבי יהודה differently is given in the continuation.

keyTerms.meaning: No: opens a rejection of the proposed proof

phrases.english: No, Rabbi Yehuda
phrases.notes: The sentence keeps going on the next amud, where the גמרא finishes explaining רבי יהודה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins to reject the proof from רבי יהודה in Step 15.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from רבי יהודה's statement.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It is not certain that רבי יהודה is referring to the same case as the תנא קמא. The full reason comes in the continuation.
